title: Memorisation vs. in-context lookup (canonical vs. random order)
question: How do in-distribution sample efficiency and minimum required depth compare across a fixed canonical alphabet (`symbol_set=decimal` or `hex`, `resample_alphabet=False`, `symbol_pool_size=None`, where static weight memorisation is possible and the `B^L` problem universe overlaps between train and eval at small B, L), per-problem shuffled canonical glyphs (`symbol_set=decimal` or `hex`, `symbol_pool_size=B`, `resample_alphabet=True`—setting `symbol_pool_size=B` explicitly so `B < len(symbol_set)` keeps the exact same `B`-glyph vocabulary rather than widening to 10 or 16 glyphs), and random 240-byte alphabets? (Zero-shot transfer to OOD permuted canonical alphabets after canonical exposure is tested in `addition/prior-override`.)
